decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary consumable for the firm’s wood-floor business, its market potential is still uncertain after only one year, so keeping the option open is sensible.
Maintenance oil fits closely with the firm’s flooring offering and is relatively inexpensive to continue offering while demand information is still emerging.

This care product is more niche and somewhat overlapping with the other floor-care items, but the firm would likely retain it another year because learning about demand is still valuable and carrying costs are limited.
A moisture-protection underlay is a natural add-on to flooring sales, and the firm would likely keep it on the market while it assesses customer uptake and bundling potential.
High-density underlay foam is a useful adjacent product but may face overlap with other underlays, so there is some rationalization risk even though the option is still worth keeping open.

Oak parquet is strategically close to the firm’s core business, but because it likely ties up more inventory and commercial effort than the accessory products, its downside risk is somewhat higher despite being worth retaining for now.
